memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance, since the food offerings presented to the Lord, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as he promised them - Josh 13:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Every tribe received a portion of land — except one. The tribe of Levi, set apart for the service of God, was given no territory at all. At first this might sound like they were left out, overlooked, given less than the others. But the reason turns everything upside down: the Lord Himself was their inheritance.

While the other tribes received fields and towns, the Levites received something far greater — a special nearness to God, a life devoted to His service and worship. Elsewhere it is put beautifully: "The Lord is my portion" (Lam 3:24; Num 18:20). What could be richer than that? The Levites teach us that the best inheritance is not things but God Himself.

It is easy to measure our lives by what we have — property, security, possessions. But the deepest riches are found in knowing God. Paul, who lost everything the world counts valuable, called it all rubbish compared to the surpassing worth of knowing Christ (Phil 3:8). The Levites had no land, yet they had the Lord, and that was more than enough. In Christ, every believer now shares in this inheritance — we are all brought near to God, made a royal priesthood, given God Himself as our greatest treasure (1 Pet 2:9).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you truly regard God Himself as your greatest inheritance?
- How would your life change if you measured your riches by nearness to God?
- What "land" are you tempted to prize above the Lord who gives it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for prizing things above knowing You. You are my portion and my greatest treasure. Help me to find my truest riches in You alone. Amen.
